characters.description: The practical, kind-hearted Kansas girl who once traveled to Oz, now on a sea voyage with her Uncle Henry when a storm sweeps her overboard. Washed up alone in a strange fairy country, she keeps her courage and good sense amid marvels and dangers, making friends easily and facing threats with steady nerve. Her earlier adventures have given her a fondness for magical lands, and she soon finds herself caught up in a new quest.
characters.name: Dorothy

characters.description: A yellow hen who is swept ashore in the same storm as Dorothy and, in this fairy country, turns out to be able to talk. Tart, opinionated, and shrewd, she is a practical companion who grumbles and argues but proves clever and brave when it matters. She becomes Dorothy's constant friend through the adventure.
characters.name: Billina

characters.description: A round copper mechanical man found standing motionless in a rocky place, who runs by clockwork and must be wound up separately for thinking, speaking, and moving. Not truly alive but faithful and dependable when wound, he serves as a guardian and helper to Dorothy, though he tends to run down at inconvenient moments and needs rewinding.
characters.name: Tik-Tok

characters.description: The vain and imperious princess who rules the land of Ev in the absence of its royal family. She owns a cabinet of thirty beautiful interchangeable heads, which she swaps to suit her mood, and she is quick to anger and cruelty. When she covets Dorothy's head for her collection, she becomes a dangerous threat to the young traveler.
characters.name: Princess Langwidere

characters.description: The young and gracious girl ruler of the land of Oz, wise and kind beyond her years. Learning of the plight of the enslaved royal family of neighboring Ev, she leads an expedition across the deadly desert with her army and her closest friends to attempt a rescue. Gentle but resolute, she guides the quest with fairness and courage.
characters.name: Ozma

characters.description: The clever, good-natured man made of straw, proud of the brains the Wizard once gave him, and one of Ozma's most trusted companions. He joins her rescue party across the desert, ready to puzzle out problems and stand by his friends in danger.
characters.name: The Scarecrow

characters.description: The kind and sentimental man made of tin, who treasures his heart and keeps himself polished bright. A loyal friend of Ozma and the Scarecrow, he comes along on the expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev, gentle in feeling but steadfast in a crisis.
characters.name: The Tin Woodman

characters.description: The great Lion who once feared his own timidity but has become a brave and noble friend to Dorothy and the others. He helps draw Ozma's royal chariot on the journey and lends his strength and courage to the rescue, still quick to admit his fears even as he faces them.
characters.name: The Cowardly Lion

characters.description: A huge tiger, companion to the Cowardly Lion, who complains constantly of a ravenous appetite and longs to eat a fat baby, yet whose tender conscience will never let him actually harm anything. Gentle beneath his fearsome talk, he too helps pull Ozma's chariot and guard her company.
characters.name: The Hungry Tiger

characters.description: The rich and crafty king of the underground Nomes, ruler of a vast mountain kingdom of caverns and treasure. He holds the royal family of Ev captive, having transformed them by magic into ornaments hidden among his countless possessions. Sly and treacherous, he sets cruel bargains and traps for those who come to challenge him.
characters.name: The Nome King

recaps.ending: The rescue succeeds through cleverness rather than force. After many of the party fail the Nome King's guessing game and are themselves turned into ornaments, the yellow hen Billina, who has been quietly eavesdropping, learns the secret of which ornaments the captives are and how to identify them. When the Nome King turns treacherous, the Nomes' deadly fear of eggs, which Billina wields against them, breaks his power. All the transformed prisoners, the royal family of Ev and Dorothy's own enchanted friends alike, are restored to their proper forms, and the Nome King is defeated. Dorothy takes possession of his Magic Belt, a powerful magical device. The royal family of Ev is freed and its rightful king restored, and everyone travels to the Emerald City for a joyous celebration. When it is time to go, Ozma uses her magic to send Dorothy safely back to her Uncle Henry, promising that she can watch over Dorothy and bring her to Oz again whenever she is truly needed. The friends part happily, the adventure won.
recaps.in_short: On a sea voyage with her Uncle Henry, Dorothy is swept overboard in a storm and washed up in the fairy land of Ev with a talking yellow hen, Billina. Exploring, they meet the wheeled Wheelers and discover Tik-Tok, a copper clockwork man who serves them. They come to the palace of vain Princess Langwidere, who collects interchangeable heads and threatens to take Dorothy's. Rescue arrives when Ozma, the young ruler of Oz, crosses the deadly desert with her army and friends, the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Cowardly Lion, and Hungry Tiger, to free the royal family of Ev, whom the Nome King has transformed into ornaments and hidden in his mountain. The Nome King challenges the rescuers to guess which ornaments the captives are, turning those who fail into ornaments themselves, and several friends are lost this way. But Billina secretly learns his secret, the Nomes' terror of eggs saves the day, and the transformed family and friends are all restored. Dorothy wins the Nome King's Magic Belt, everyone celebrates in Oz, and she is sent safely home.

recaps.text: Earlier in the series: A Kansas girl named Dorothy was carried by a cyclone to the magical land of Oz, where, with a Scarecrow, a Tin Woodman, and a Cowardly Lion, she sought the great Wizard's help, destroyed the Wicked Witch of the West, exposed the Wizard as a humbug, and finally returned home, leaving the Scarecrow to rule the Emerald City. After the Wizard's departure, a boy named Tip fled the witch Mombi with living companions and, with the help of Glinda the Good, was revealed to be the Emerald City's rightful ruler, a princess who had been magically hidden in a boy's form. Restored to herself as Princess Ozma, she took the throne of Oz. This book follows Dorothy on a new voyage and the young Queen Ozma on a rescue mission to a neighboring fairyland.

Sailing across the ocean with her Uncle Henry, Dorothy is swept overboard during a fierce storm and drifts to shore in the strange fairy country of Ev, accompanied by a yellow hen who, in this land, can talk and whom Dorothy names Billina. Exploring the shore, the two encounter the alarming Wheelers, creatures with wheels instead of hands and feet, and take refuge until they discover a curious copper man standing motionless among the rocks. He is Tik-Tok, a mechanical man who runs by clockwork and must be wound up to think, speak, and move. Once wound, Tik-Tok becomes their protector and guide, and the little party sets out to learn more about the land they have washed up in.

Dorothy, Billina, and Tik-Tok reach the palace of Ev and meet its ruler in the royal family's absence, the vain Princess Langwidere, who owns a cabinet of thirty interchangeable heads and swaps them at whim. When Langwidere covets Dorothy's head for her collection and threatens to take it, Dorothy is in real danger. Rescue arrives in the form of Ozma, the young ruler of Oz, who has crossed the deadly desert with her army and her friends, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, the Cowardly Lion, and the Hungry Tiger, on a mission of mercy. Ozma has come to free the royal family of Ev, who have been enslaved by the powerful Nome King. Joining forces, the companions set out for the Nome King's mountain to attempt the rescue.

At the Nome King's underground kingdom, the crafty ruler reveals that he has transformed the captive royal family of Ev into ornaments and scattered them, disguised, among the countless treasures of his palace. He offers the rescuers a cruel bargain: each may enter and guess which ornaments are the enchanted prisoners, but anyone who guesses wrong will themselves be turned into an ornament. One by one, several of the would-be rescuers try, fail, and are transformed, and the situation grows dire. Meanwhile the resourceful hen Billina, small and overlooked, hides and secretly overhears the Nome King, gathering the crucial knowledge of how to tell which ornaments are the captives, knowledge that may yet turn the tide.

Armed with the secret she overheard, Billina exposes which ornaments hold the enchanted captives, and when the Nome King turns treacherous, the Nomes' deadly terror of eggs, which Billina uses against them, shatters his power. All the transformed prisoners, the royal family of Ev and Dorothy's own enchanted friends, are restored to their true shapes, and the Nome King is beaten. Dorothy claims his powerful Magic Belt as a prize. The royal family of Ev is freed and its rightful king set back on the throne, and the whole company travels to the Emerald City for a grand celebration. When the time comes to part, Ozma uses her magic to return Dorothy safely to her Uncle Henry, promising to watch over her and bring her back to Oz whenever she is needed. The adventure ends in triumph and friendship.

characters.description: The Invalid boy who lived in Portland under a forged identity, who showed Lena the Wilds and the truth about the cured cities, and who stayed on the city side of the border fence so that she could get over it. Lena heard the guards fire as she ran, and has believed since that he died there.
characters.name: Alex Sheathes

characters.description: The girl who went over the fence out of Portland and did not die in the Wilds. The book follows her in two threads. In the earlier one she is newly arrived on the wrong side of the border, sick, starving and grieving, with no idea how to survive outside a city. In the later one she is living in New York under the name Lena Morgan Jones, posing as a cured student, working for the resistance, and unrecognisable to anyone who knew the careful girl she used to be: harder, colder, and trained to do what she is told.
characters.name: Lena Haloway

characters.description: The leader of a homesteader camp in the Wilds who finds Lena at the border and keeps her alive. Practical to the point of ruthlessness, she runs her people by strict rules, the first of which is that the past is dead and nobody talks about who they were before. She has no patience for grief and a great deal of patience for teaching someone to be useful.
characters.name: Raven

characters.description: The eighteen-year-old son of the man who founded Deliria-Free America, the movement campaigning for the cure to be given earlier and to everybody. He appears at DFA events as its model young believer, and he has publicly committed to undergoing the procedure himself even though a condition in his brain makes it likely to kill or disable him. Composed, courteous and entirely certain of what he has been raised to believe.
characters.name: Julian Fineman

characters.description: Julian's father and the head of Deliria-Free America, a movement that has grown powerful enough to shape government policy. He is a public man who speaks about sacrifice for the cause, and he raised his son to be its proof.
characters.name: Thomas Fineman

characters.description: Raven's partner in the homestead: blunt, hard to read, and dismissive of Lena at first. He does the work nobody else wants and says almost nothing about himself.
characters.name: Tack

characters.description: A small girl living with the homesteaders, born on the wrong side of the fence and never registered as a person by anyone. Lena helps look after her, and finds in her the first thing in the Wilds she can care about.
characters.name: Blue

characters.description: One of the homesteaders, easygoing and quick to joke, and among the first people in the camp to treat Lena as company rather than a burden.
characters.name: Hunter

recaps.ending: Lena and Julian get out of the tunnels together, and Julian, who was raised to believe the cure was the only safe future, chooses her and the uncured world instead. His father does not take him back. Julian is publicly disowned by Deliria-Free America and written out of it, which leaves him with nothing except the resistance and Lena, and the two of them are together at the close. Lena has stopped being the survivor who does what Raven tells her and made a decision of her own for the first time since she came over the fence. Then, in the last moments of the book, Raven brings someone into the room: Alex, alive. He did not die at the Portland fence. He was taken, held, and has come out of it, and when he looks at Lena he behaves as though she is nobody to him. The reunion Lena spent a year mourning for arrives with everything about it wrong, and it lands on the same day she committed herself to Julian.
recaps.in_short: The story runs in two threads. In the earlier one, Lena crosses into the Wilds after Alex's death at the Portland fence, is found half dead by a woman called Raven, and is taken into a homesteader camp where she is taught to survive under the rule that the past is dead. A brutal winter kills the youngest of them, and the survivors walk south to New York. In the later thread, Lena lives in the city under a false name as a cured student and works for the resistance, assigned to watch Julian Fineman, son of the head of Deliria-Free America, who has agreed to undergo a procedure that will probably kill him. A DFA rally is attacked and the two of them are seized and imprisoned underground. In captivity Julian's certainty collapses, his father refuses to save him, and Lena, who was supposed to feel nothing, escapes and goes back for him. They get out, Julian is disowned by the movement, and the two of them come together. In the final scene Alex walks in, alive, and does not acknowledge her.

recaps.text: Previously: in a United States that classifies love as the disease amor deliria nervosa, every citizen is cured at eighteen by a procedure that removes the ability to feel it, after which the government assigns them a spouse, a career and a number of children. Seventeen-year-old Lena Haloway of Portland, Maine wanted the cure: her mother had died of the disease and the family lived under the suspicion that came with it. Then she met Alex, a laboratory guard with a procedure scar who turned out to be an Invalid, born uncured in the Wilds beyond the border fence and living in the city under a dead boy's identity. He showed her the settlements outside, and everything she had been taught came apart. Lena fell in love, discovered that her mother had not killed herself but had been imprisoned for years in the Crypts and had escaped, and agreed to run with Alex into the Wilds. They were caught, Lena was locked in her room with her procedure brought forward, and her small cousin Grace helped her get free. Alex got her over the border fence and stayed behind to hold the guards off. Lena ran into the Wilds hearing gunfire, alone and certain he was dead.

The book alternates between two times. In the later thread, Lena is in New York City living as Lena Morgan Jones, a cured student with forged papers and a false scar, placed there by the resistance. Her assignment is Deliria-Free America, the movement demanding that the cure be given to everyone and given younger, and specifically its founder's son, Julian Fineman, who speaks at its events. She is competent, watchful and closed off, and nothing about her resembles the girl who left Portland. In the earlier thread, that girl comes over the border fence half dead, with no food, no shelter and no idea how to live outside a city. She collapses in the Wilds and is found by Raven, who drags her back from the edge of dying and takes her into a homesteader camp, where the first rule she is given is that whoever she was before does not exist any more.

In the Wilds, Lena slowly recovers and is put to work. The homesteaders live in an abandoned building on scavenged supplies, and everyone earns their place; Raven runs it with hard rules, Tack does the work nobody wants, and among the others are a small girl called Blue and a friendly older boy called Hunter. Lena is not allowed to grieve out loud, and learns to hunt, to walk long distances, and to stop expecting anything. In New York, Lena attends a DFA rally where Julian speaks. He tells the crowd he will undergo the procedure himself despite a condition that makes it likely to kill him, offering himself as proof of the movement's conviction. The rally is attacked by Scavengers, a violent faction from outside the cities, and in the chaos Lena and Julian are both seized and taken.

Lena and Julian are held underground in the tunnels beneath the city, locked in a cell together with no idea what their captors want. Julian has never spent a day among the uncured, and being shut in with one who argues with him begins to unpick the certainty he was raised on; he starts asking questions rather than reciting answers. In the earlier thread, winter closes over the homestead. There is not enough food and no medicine, people get sick, and the camp is reduced to endurance. Blue dies in it. The loss finishes whatever was left of Lena's old self, and when Raven decides that the camp cannot survive where it is and that they must walk south, Lena goes without arguing, because there is nothing behind her worth turning around for.

The march south is long and takes more from the group; by the end of it Lena is somebody who can keep walking through anything. They reach New York, where the resistance takes them in, and Lena is given papers, a name that is not hers and a place inside a cured city as an agent. That is how she came to be watching Julian Fineman. In the tunnels, captivity drags on. Demands are put to Julian's father, and the answer that comes back is that Thomas Fineman will not trade anything for his son: a boy who dies for the cause is worth more to Deliria-Free America than a boy who is ransomed. Julian is told he is going to be executed. Lena, who was sent to observe him and nothing else, finds that she cannot leave him where he is.

Lena gets out of the cell and, instead of running, goes back through the tunnels for Julian. They escape together in the dark with the Scavengers behind them, and along the way Lena stops pretending: she tells him she is uncured, that she came from the Wilds, and that everything the DFA taught him about people like her is wrong. Julian, whose father has just left him to die for the movement, has nothing to defend any more. They come up out of the tunnels into the city together, hunted by both sides, and by the time they surface Julian has refused the procedure he had publicly promised to undergo, and Lena has broken every instruction the resistance gave her.

The resistance recovers them and gets them off the streets. In the aftermath it becomes clear how little of what happened was chance, and how completely Thomas Fineman was prepared to spend his son: a martyred Julian served the movement better than a living one, and the DFA moves quickly to write him out. Julian is publicly disowned and treated as dead by the organisation he was raised to represent, which leaves him with no name, no family and nowhere to go except with Lena and the people she works for. Lena, who has spent a year following Raven's rule that the past is dead, admits to herself that she has chosen something for the first time since Portland, and the two of them come together.

Lena and Julian settle into the resistance's safe house with the DFA hunting them both and the movement's grip on the cured cities tightening. Julian has cut himself off from everything he was raised in and has only Lena and this side of the fence now, and Lena, who arrived in the Wilds a year ago with nothing, has become someone who makes her own decisions about who she keeps. Then Raven brings a new arrival into the room, and it is Alex. He is alive: he did not die at the Portland fence but was taken, held, and has come out changed. He looks at Lena as if she is a stranger and says nothing to her at all. Everything Lena built out of believing him dead, including Julian, is standing in the room with her when he walks in.

characters.description: An itinerant former Army officer travelling from Maine toward San Diego. He changes course for Laconia after recognizing it as the New Hampshire birthplace attributed to his late father, Stan Reacher.
characters.name: Jack Reacher

characters.description: A Canadian sawmill worker travelling with her boyfriend, Shorty Fleck, to sell valuable property in New York. She reads the map during their back-road detour and reaches an isolated motel after their Honda overheats.
characters.name: Patty Sundstrom

characters.description: A Canadian potato farmer travelling with his girlfriend, Patty Sundstrom. Their plan to sell valuables in New York is interrupted when their aging Honda overheats and they seek help at a remote motel.
characters.name: Shorty Fleck

characters.description: The late father Jack Reacher believes was born in Laconia and left the area at seventeen. The chance discovery of that claimed birthplace prompts Reacher to investigate the family's local history.
characters.name: Stan Reacher

characters.description: The polished receptionist who appears to lead the group managing the isolated motel. He and three associates present themselves as investors and question Patty and Shorty about their journey.
characters.name: Mark

characters.description: One of Mark's three associates at the remote property. He is introduced as a fellow investor when the group hosts Patty and Shorty for dinner.
characters.name: Robert

characters.description: One of the men presented as an investor in the isolated motel. He joins Mark, Robert, and Peter at dinner with the stranded Canadian couple.
characters.name: Stephen

characters.description: A member of Mark's motel group who is presented as one of the property's investors. He is said to handle the quad bikes kept at the site.
characters.name: Peter

characters.description: A Laconia city-records employee who helps Reacher search for evidence of his father's family. Her initial property search finds no Reacher household in the city during the relevant period.
characters.name: Elizabeth Castle

characters.description: A Laconia town attorney and census enthusiast whom Elizabeth Castle recommends when the expected Reacher household cannot be found in local records.
characters.name: Carter Carrington

characters.description: Laconia's chief of detectives. He brings Reacher into the police department's historical-record search for an old report involving the Reacher surname.
characters.name: Jim Shaw

characters.description: A Laconia detective and former Army MP who assists Reacher with the department's historical files. Their shared military background is apparent when he recognizes her professional experience.
characters.name: Brenda Amos

characters.description: The motel leader previously known as Mark. A police record gives his name as Mark Reacher and identifies him as a young motel renovator involved in a dispute over a delayed permit, creating a possible link to Jack Reacher's family search.
characters.name: Mark Reacher

characters.description: Stan Reacher's father, found in county census records at rented housing in Ryantown. He worked first as a tin-mill foreman and later grading roads.
characters.name: James Reacher

characters.description: Stan Reacher's mother, recorded with James and Stan in Ryantown rather than Laconia. The censuses list her first as a bedsheet finisher and later without employment.
characters.name: Elizabeth Reacher

characters.description: A Macedonian mechanic whom Mark contacts about the stranded Honda. Speaking by phone, he promises Patty and Shorty that he will bring the needed repair part within several hours.
characters.name: Karel

characters.description: A local resident who keeps archived material about Ryantown, including a newsletter concerning the former settlement and an unsuccessful campaign over alleged groundwater pollution.
characters.name: Bruce Jones

characters.description: A Laconia patrolman briefed by Brenda Amos about the threat to Reacher. He recognizes Reacher during an early-morning street encounter and takes him voluntarily to the police station for protection.
characters.name: Davison

characters.description: An elderly resident of an assisted-living facility whose memories of Ryantown may help Reacher understand his family's years in the vanished mill settlement.
characters.name: Mortimer

characters.description: The gray-ponytailed former clergyman who drives Reacher to meet Mortimer. He has been between parishes for decades and serves as Reacher's local guide during the Ryantown inquiry.
characters.name: Reverend Patrick G. Burke

characters.description: The name Peter uses while posing as the front-desk man at the supposedly closed motel. He tells Reacher and Burke that the property is under repair and drives them back to the blocked county road.
characters.name: Tony Kelly

characters.description: The motel owner and hunt organizer previously identified as Mark Reacher. After Reacher disarms him on the forest track, he gives his actual surname as Breacher, ending the apparent family connection.
characters.name: Mark Breacher

characters.description: A living Laconia resident whom Brenda Amos locates during the family inquiry. He agrees to meet Jack Reacher immediately, despite Reacher having long believed that the Stan Reacher he sought was his late father.
characters.name: Stan Reacher

characters.description: Jack Reacher's father, first known as Bill. The living Stan Reacher identifies him as a childhood cousin who borrowed Stan's birth certificate after killing a local bully, then enlisted in the Marines under the Reacher identity.
characters.name: William Reacher

recaps.ending: The motel operation collapses after Patty and Shorty set the property on fire and resist the hunters. Shorty suffers a grave thigh wound, but Patty keeps him alive until Reacher reaches them. Mark kills Stephen, Robert, and Peter to erase witnesses, then kills Karel to obtain the tow-truck key. Reacher disarms and kills Mark. Patty and Shorty depart in Mark's Mercedes to seek treatment, carrying their comics and roughly a million dollars from the hunt. The operation's known participants are dead. Amos reports that the Boston cleanup operative has withdrawn. The living Stan Reacher explains that Reacher's father was his cousin Bill, later William Reacher, who used Stan's birth certificate to join the Marines after killing the local bully. Carrington and Castle, feared missing, are safely camping together at the old Ryantown site. Reacher chooses not to pursue the unknown people who once sent his father birthday cards. With the family mystery and immediate danger resolved, he leaves alone for San Diego.
recaps.in_short: While travelling from Maine toward San Diego, Jack Reacher detours to Laconia to investigate the birthplace attributed to his father. Nearby, Canadians Patty Sundstrom and Shorty Fleck are trapped at a false motel and selected as prey for a paid human hunt. Reacher's research and the couple's captivity converge at the remote property. Patty and Shorty burn the motel, fight back, and survive, although Shorty is badly wounded. They and Reacher overcome the hunters, and Reacher kills Mark Breacher, the organizer who had appeared to share Reacher's surname. The couple leaves with their valuable comics and the operation's cash. Reacher then learns that his father was Bill, later William Reacher, who borrowed his cousin Stan Reacher's birth certificate after killing a bully and enlisted in the Marines under that identity. Carter Carrington and Elizabeth Castle are found safe together, and Reacher resumes his journey toward San Diego.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Reacher is an itinerant former Army officer who travels without a settled home.

Reacher is travelling from coastal Maine toward San Diego when a rural fork prompts a detour to Laconia, the birthplace attributed to his late father, Stan Reacher. Local property and census searches initially find no trace of the family. Elizabeth Castle directs him to census specialist Carter Carrington, and police officers Jim Shaw and Brenda Amos help locate a 1943 report. It says Stan was present when another youth beat a local bully, but Stan himself ran from the confrontation. Meanwhile, Canadian couple Patty Sundstrom and Shorty Fleck reach an isolated motel after their Honda overheats. Mark and his associates Robert, Stephen, and Peter claim to be investors, yet their explanations grow increasingly troubling. The room has no communications, its door sometimes refuses to open, and the promised mechanic remains unavailable. Unknown to the couple, the men can control the lock remotely and watch them through concealed cameras. After establishing that nobody knows where Patty and Shorty are, the group decides they are suitable for an undisclosed purpose and alerts an outside contact.

A police record identifies the motel leader as Mark Reacher, suggesting a possible connection to Jack Reacher's family inquiry. County records finally place James, Elizabeth, and Stan Reacher in Ryantown, a vanished mill settlement outside Laconia. Mark learns that Reacher is searching for the old family address. At the motel, Patty finds evidence contradicting the claim that their room is newly refurbished. She and Shorty move their luggage toward the road using a quad bike, only to discover that the motel sign has vanished and that their hosts have recovered the hidden bags. Patty's mechanical knowledge exposes further contradictions in the alleged Honda fault. Karel arrives with a tow truck and confirms that the battery feed was deliberately cut. He appears willing to remove the couple, but never returns after sending them inside. Their door locks and the blind closes, leaving them physically imprisoned. Elsewhere, Reacher protects a bar worker from an attacker and is warned by Brenda Amos and Jim Shaw that the man's criminally connected father may send violent associates after him. Reacher nevertheless continues toward Ryantown.

Karel joins Mark's group after posing as an independent mechanic, confirming that the failed rescue was staged. Patty deduces that the room is under audio surveillance and that the captors have tailored their deceptions around private conversations. Reacher reaches Ryantown with a local researcher and locates the former family home, but clashes with an orchard family paid to keep the researcher away. Back in Laconia, Carter Carrington and Elizabeth Castle continue helping with the historical puzzle. Reacher also faces retaliation from the orchard group and a separate Massachusetts operation linked to the man he injured while defending the bar worker. Police shelter him while tracking an obvious decoy vehicle, but a disguised van slips away and reaches the remote motel. Wealthy men using false identities begin arriving there and inspecting Patty and Shorty through the window. Reacher meets Mortimer, an elderly Ryantown witness, with help from Reverend Patrick G. Burke. Mortimer remembers Stan and a visiting cousin as close birdwatchers, though he cannot reliably tell them apart. He directs Reacher to old bird-club records. Patty and Shorty now know that strangers are evaluating them while the motel group watches their every move.

Bird-club records show that S. Reacher and W. Reacher jointly reported a rare hawk over Ryantown. A university ornithologist related to both contributors offers a possible route to identifying the second boy. Reacher defeats three men attempting to seize him in the library, then returns to Ryantown and overcomes another group assembled by the orchard family. At the motel, six paying customers gather. Karel is the final participant, receiving favorable terms because he helped deceive the captives. Room 10 proves to be a reinforced prison that blocks both escape and radio signals. Brenda Amos reports that Carter Carrington and Elizabeth Castle are missing, while a professor claims Stan Reacher is alive. Reacher and Burke find the motel road blocked by Karel's tow truck and visit the property. Peter, using the name Tony Kelly, presents a coordinated cover story, but vehicle records and the false contractor explanation convince Reacher that someone is being held there. Peter tells Patty and Shorty that they must flee through the forest. Mark then states the truth: six customers have paid to hunt them with bows, night vision, and quad bikes. As the door unlocks and the hunt begins, Reacher enters the forest alone.

Patty and Shorty initially become lost in the woods, unaware that their flashlights contain tracking devices. They return to the motel and turn the captors' sabotage against them, using fuel from the parked vehicles to set the property ablaze. The fire destroys the operation's cameras and communications and spoils the hunters' night vision. Shorty kills one hunter before another shoots him through the thigh. Patty kills that attacker, treats Shorty's likely fractured leg, and goes in search of transport. Reacher kills or defeats the hunters he encounters. With the enterprise collapsing, Mark murders Stephen, Robert, and Peter, burns the remaining buildings, and tries to flee with the cash and false identities. Karel continues hunting Patty, but Mark shoots him to obtain the tow-truck key. Reacher arrives before Mark can kill Patty, disarms him, and forces him to reveal that his surname is Breacher rather than Reacher. When Patty declines to execute their captor, Reacher kills Breacher himself. Reacher and Patty recover Shorty. The couple retains its valuable comics and receives roughly a million dollars found in Breacher's Mercedes, then prepares to leave for urgent medical treatment.

Reacher clears the tow truck from the access road, and Patty and Shorty drive south in Breacher's Mercedes with their comics and the hunters' cash. Shorty remains in need of urgent treatment, but both have escaped the destroyed operation. Brenda Amos reports that the Boston cleanup operative has returned home, though Carter Carrington and Elizabeth Castle are still missing. She has also found a living man named Stan Reacher. This Stan explains that he is not Jack Reacher's father. He grew up in Ryantown as the son of James and Elizabeth Reacher, alongside a cousin named Bill. Bill was the other young birdwatcher, defended Stan from the local bully, and later killed that man. To conceal his identity and enlist in the Marines, Bill borrowed Stan's birth certificate. Bill subsequently became William Reacher, married Josephine, and had two sons, including Jack. Reacher recognizes that his father's history was concealed by the borrowed identity rather than by a different parentage. At Ryantown, he finds Carrington and Castle alive, together, and voluntarily camping at the former family site. After they reassure Amos, Reacher ends his inquiries and resumes hitchhiking alone toward San Diego.

characters.description: Chicago's wizard, the Winter Knight, warden of Demonreach - and, these days, a father trying to build something like a normal life with his daughter Maggie. When the Fomor propose peace talks to the assembled supernatural nations, Mab drafts Harry as Winter's muscle for the conference. Then his brother commits an unforgivable crime in front of everyone, and Harry has to choose between the duties everyone can see and the loyalty he can never explain.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: Harry's half-brother, a vampire of the White Court, their kinship still a closely held secret. Thomas has been steadier since Justine's pregnancy was confirmed - which makes it inexplicable when he attempts to assassinate the king of the svartalves on the eve of the peace conference, an act of war under the Accords. Captured and beaten nearly to death, he will not say why he did it, even to his brother.
characters.name: Thomas Raith

characters.description: Thomas's beloved - a onetime thrall of the White Court whose long recovery left her able to survive a vampire's love. She is pregnant with Thomas's child, news that reshapes both brothers' worlds. When Thomas is taken, Justine's desperation becomes one of the engines of the book: whatever it costs, whoever must be bargained with, she wants him back.
characters.name: Justine

characters.description: Formerly of Chicago PD, still recovering from the injuries Nicodemus gave her - a shattered knee and arm that ended her fighting career as she knew it. She and Harry are finally, properly together. Sidelined from the front line but not from the fight, Murphy applies what she has always had: nerve, judgment, and an absolute refusal to be protected out of relevance.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: Warden Commander of the White Council's western American territories and one of Harry's few genuine friends inside the Council. Carlos arrives with the delegation for the peace talks - and with bad news delivered as friendship: the Council's patience with Harry Dresden is exhausted, and powerful voices want him expelled. The conference forces Carlos to weigh that friendship against duties Harry keeps giving him reasons to doubt.
characters.name: Carlos Ramirez

characters.description: Senior Council member, the Council's sanctioned assassin, Harry's old mentor - and his grandfather, a secret shared between them but not with the world. Ebenezar comes to Chicago for the talks and for family reasons of his own, carrying a lifetime of hatred for the White Court, whose kind destroyed people he loved. He does not know Thomas Raith is his grandson, and that ignorance is a loaded weapon lying between him and Harry.
characters.name: Ebenezar McCoy

characters.description: Effective ruler of the White Court of vampires, reigning through her puppet father. Lara is brilliant, patient, and dangerous in every register from boardroom to battlefield. Winter owes her two favors - a debt Mab has assigned Harry to pay - and the crisis around Thomas gives Lara every reason to spend them. Her interests and Harry's align exactly as far as she wants them to.
characters.name: Lara Raith

characters.description: The Winter Lady - Harry's former apprentice, now several years into a queenship she never asked for. Molly moves through the conference as Winter's poised, formidable young queen, her mantle's power worn like tailored armor, while the Carpenter family still does not know what their daughter has become. She lives under svartalf patronage, which places her uncomfortably close to the book's inciting crime.
characters.name: Molly Carpenter

characters.description: The Queen of Air and Darkness, attending the peace conference as one of its presiding powers. Mab's agenda runs, as always, several layers deep: the security of the Accords, the debts she owes and collects, and the positioning of her Knight - whom she volunteers for duties that serve purposes she does not explain. Her instructions to Harry about Lara Raith are exact and non-negotiable.
characters.name: Mab

characters.description: King of the svartalves - the ancient, scrupulous artisan folk hosting the peace conference at their Chicago embassy. Etri is a being of stone-hard honor and long memory; his people's hospitality is sacred to them, and the attempt on his life under his own roof is an offense their law answers with death. He is not cruel, but he is utterly unbending.
characters.name: Etri

characters.description: The last of the Titans, walking out of humanity's oldest nightmares into a Chicago conference room - an immortal of world-breaking power, bearing the Eye of Balor. Ethniu arrives with the Fomor delegation, and it becomes clear the talks were never the point: she has come to deliver a declaration, and she considers the assembled nations of the Accords beneath fear.
characters.name: Ethniu

recaps.ending: The peace talks end with a declaration of war. Ethniu, the Last Titan, bearing the Eye of Balor and backed by King Corb's Fomor, stands before the assembled Accords nations and announces her contempt for their order and her intent: Chicago will be destroyed as her first demonstration, its people made an example to humanity. The conference shatters; the powers must choose overnight between scattering and standing, and the book closes on the eve of battle, flowing directly into Battle Ground. The Thomas crisis is parked, not solved: after his inexplicable attempt to assassinate Etri, Harry and Lara broke him out of svartalf custody - fighting through, among others, Ebenezar McCoy, whose hatred of the White Court turned the intercept into a savage grandfather-against-grandson battle that neither fully understands, since Ebenezar still does not know Thomas is his grandson. Thomas, dying from his injuries, was taken by Harry to Demonreach and placed in the island's crystalline stasis - alive, beyond rescue or execution, with his motive still unexplained and Justine, pregnant, waiting. Harry's ties are fraying everywhere: the White Council moves toward expelling him, Ramirez's friendship has curdled into professional suspicion, the rift with his grandfather is open and bleeding, and Winter's debt has bound him to Lara Raith's interests. Murphy, half-healed, arms herself anyway. The Titan's ultimatum hangs over all of it.
recaps.in_short: The Fomor propose peace talks with the supernatural nations, hosted by the svartalves in Chicago, and Mab drafts Harry as Winter's security - while assigning him to repay Winter's two favors owed to Lara Raith. Thomas and Justine are expecting a child; the White Council is moving to expel Harry; and then Thomas, without explanation, attempts to assassinate Etri, king of the svartalves, and is captured and held for a death sentence under Accords law. Harry and Lara mount a covert extraction from the svartalf deeps that goes loud: Ebenezar McCoy - Harry's grandfather, ignorant that Thomas is also his grandson and consumed by hatred of the White Court - intercepts them, and the escape becomes a brutal fight between kin. Harry carries the dying Thomas to Demonreach and locks him in the island's stasis, saving his life at the cost of his freedom, his motive never spoken. Then the talks reveal their true purpose: the Fomor present Ethniu, the Last Titan, bearing the Eye of Balor, who declares she will destroy Chicago as a lesson to the world. The book ends on the eve of the battle, with every alliance Harry has strained to breaking.

recaps.text: Previously in the series: Harry Dresden serves Mab as the Winter Knight and wards Demonreach, the island prison for horrors. He destroyed the Red Court, died and returned, and killed the Nemesis-corrupted Winter Lady Maeve, whose mantle passed to his apprentice Molly Carpenter - now the Winter Lady, a secret her family does not share. On Mab's loan, Harry pulled a heist into the vault of Hades beside Nicodemus Archleone, which cost the Denarian his daughter and his standing; Murphy was maimed when Nicodemus broke the holy sword Fidelacchius - reborn later in the hands of Waldo Butters, the new Knight of Faith. The parasite in Harry's head proved to be Bonnie, a newborn spirit of intellect, his daughter with the departed shadow of Lasciel. Harry finally met his human daughter, Maggie, who lives with the Carpenters, and he and Murphy are together at last. His half-brother Thomas Raith of the White Court - kin known only to a few - loves Justine, long recovered from thralldom. In the wider world, the Fomor have spent years raiding humanity's coasts and snatching practitioners; the White Council mistrusts its Winter Knight more each season; Lara Raith rules the White Court through her puppet father; and Winter owes Lara two favors, a debt Mab does not intend to leave unpaid. Beneath everything, the Outsiders' contagion Nemesis has shown it can wear any face, and the Black Council remains unfound.

The book opens on the rarest thing in Harry's life: something like peace. He trains, spends time with Maggie and Mouse, minds Bonnie the skull-dwelling spirit, and navigates being genuinely together with Murphy, who is rebuilding herself around the permanent damage Nicodemus left her. The quiet breaks twice. First, joy: Thomas and Justine are expecting a child - a near-miracle for a White Court vampire and a former thrall, and Thomas asks Harry, awkwardly and sincerely, to stand as the child's family. Second, business: Warden Commander Carlos Ramirez arrives with word that the Fomor - the sea-power that has been raiding humanity for years - have proposed formal peace talks with the nations of the Unseelie Accords, to be hosted in Chicago by the svartalves. Every major power will attend. With the news comes a warning delivered as friendship: the White Council's patience with Harry is finished, and a motion to expel him is gathering votes - his Winter service, the company he keeps, and the fear he inspires have finally outweighed his record. Mab, naturally, has plans for the conference that include her Knight; and quietly, separately, she informs Harry that Winter's outstanding debt to Lara Raith - two favors - is now his to repay, on demand and without reservation.

The delegations gather and Chicago fills with monsters on their best behavior. Harry works security under Mab's eye at the svartalf embassy - the same elegant deeps where Molly keeps her apartments, and where the conference's hosts, King Etri's people, hold hospitality as sacred law. Ebenezar McCoy arrives with the Council delegation, and grandfather and grandson manage both warmth and friction: Ebenezar presses Harry about the dangerous shape of his life - Winter, the island, the White Court vampires he keeps failing to keep at arm's length - with a hatred of Lara's kind that runs deeper and more personal than politics. Then the inexplicable happens. Thomas Raith attempts to assassinate Etri - an ambush inside the svartalf embassy, against the conference's host, an act of war under the Accords - and fails. The svartalves take him alive, barely: beaten nearly to death, held in their deeps to await a justice that has only one sentence for such an offense. He will not say why he did it. Not to his captors, not to Justine, not to Harry. The brother Harry knows would never have done it - not unprovoked, not against his own child's future - and yet every witness and every fact says he did.

The conference convenes over the crisis, with the Fomor's smiling envoys and every Accords nation watching the svartalves for weakness and each other for advantage. Harry visits Thomas in captivity and finds him wrecked in body and locked shut in mind - alive mostly because svartalf law is exact about process. Justine's desperation is absolute, and Lara Raith's position is impossible in the way that suits her talents: the White Court cannot be seen to condone the attack, and cannot afford to lose Thomas either. Lara names the price of her cooperation - and begins spending the favors Winter owes her - to one end: Thomas is not going to die in the svartalf deeps. Harry, bound by Mab's debt, bound tighter by a kinship he cannot reveal, commits to the one course that betrays the fewest people he loves: get Thomas out. The planning is a conspiracy inside a peace conference - access through connections better left unnamed, timing built around the summit's ceremonies, Lara's abilities and Harry's power fitted together - while Harry stonewalls the people he most hates lying to. Ramirez, sensing the evasions, hardens from friend into investigator; Ebenezar circles the White Court entanglement with growing fury; and Murphy, sidelined and unfooled, chooses to be Harry's accomplice rather than his conscience.

The extraction goes in - and goes loud. Harry and Lara penetrate the svartalf deeps to pull Thomas out of his cell, and the escape becomes a running battle through stone corridors, embassy security, and the conference's outer defenses, burning bridges at every step: whatever mercy the svartalves' process might have allowed is gone, and Harry's part in the affair - deniable in theory - is written in wreckage. The worst of it waits at the waterline. Ebenezar McCoy intercepts the fugitives, and the confrontation Harry has dreaded arrives at full power: the old man, seeing his grandson bleeding for a White Court vampire, unleashes a lifetime of grief and hatred, and Harry - who cannot say the one sentence that might stop it, that Thomas is Ebenezar's grandson too - stands his ground. Grandfather and grandson tear the marina apart around them, a fight neither can win and neither will yield, until the Water Beetle runs for open water. Harry takes the dying Thomas where no svartalf writ, White Council warrant, or vampire court can reach: Demonreach. The island's crystalline stasis closes over his brother - not healed, not free, not executed; suspended. Alive at the price of everything else, his motive still a locked door, while Justine waits and the conference Harry has just betrayed prepares for its final sessions.

The reckoning gathers before the summit's close. Harry limps back into the conference's orbit with his alibis thin and his accounts overdrawn: the svartalves cold with grief and offense, Ramirez now treating him as a suspect wearing a friend's face, the Council's expulsion machinery grinding forward with fresh evidence of exactly the lawlessness its members fear, and Ebenezar and Harry left staring at each other across a battlefield's worth of unsaid things. Mab's verdict on her Knight's conduct is characteristically exact - the debt to Lara is being paid, whatever else burns - and Lara herself banks the outcome with professional satisfaction: Thomas lives, and Harry Dresden is now woven into White Court interests more tightly than ever. Through it all, the actual diplomacy - the Fomor's proposal, the question of what the sea-kingdom really wants after years of raids and abductions - remains strangely, deliberately unresolved; their envoys have spent the conference watching the nations perform their rivalries. The players reconvene for the closing session with every delegation's guard already exhausted by scandal. Which, it will shortly be clear, was the design. The Fomor did not come to negotiate. They came to make an announcement, and they brought someone to deliver it.

At the final session the Fomor unveil their true delegation. King Corb's procession parts for a figure out of the oldest dark of human memory: Ethniu, the Last Titan, an immortal of world-ending power, the Eye of Balor burning in her ruined face. Her address to the assembled nations is not a negotiating position; it is a sentence passed. She holds the Accords' powers in contempt - squabbling heirs of the beings her kind once were - and she declares her intent plainly: Chicago will be destroyed, tonight, as the first demonstration of the Fomor's new order, its millions made an object lesson for a humanity that has forgotten fear. The Eye's power, unleashed even in demonstration, is beyond anything the assembled monarchs can casually answer, and the conference ends not in treaty but in triage: the powers must decide, in hours, whether to abandon the city or stand and fight for it. The book closes on the brink - Mab marshaling Winter, the nations choosing sides, Marcone's forces arming, Murphy strapping her weapons over her braces, and Harry standing between his city and a Titan, with his brother in stasis, his grandfather estranged, his Council preparing to disown him, and the battle for Chicago about to begin. The story continues, the same night, in Battle Ground.

characters.description: A seventeen-year-old demigod son of Poseidon and a veteran of many quests, now a high-school senior in New York. Loyal, wry, and battle-tested, he has set his sights on attending New Rome University alongside his girlfriend Annabeth, only to learn that he must earn three letters of recommendation from the gods to be admitted, which means taking on new tasks for Olympus whether he likes it or not.
characters.name: Percy Jackson

characters.description: A demigod daughter of Athena, Percy's brilliant and strategic girlfriend and his partner on countless adventures. A gifted planner and architect-in-the-making, she is determined to reach New Rome University with Percy and lends her sharp mind to the quest he is drawn into.
characters.name: Annabeth Chase

characters.description: A satyr and Percy's oldest friend, now an important figure among the nature spirits. Loyal and easily rattled but brave when it counts, he joins Percy and Annabeth once again to help track down what has been lost.
characters.name: Grover Underwood

characters.description: Percy's devoted mother, warm and steady, now a published writer married to Paul Blofis. She has always supported her son through the dangers of his demigod life and continues to offer him a loving home base.
characters.name: Sally Jackson

characters.description: Percy's stepfather, a kind and patient high-school English teacher who married Sally and has come to accept the strange, dangerous truth of his stepson's world.
characters.name: Paul Blofis

characters.description: The beautiful cupbearer of the gods, who serves the Olympians at their feasts. Anxious and secretive, he comes to Percy because the gods' sacred chalice has gone missing on his watch, and he needs it recovered quietly before the other gods discover the loss and blame him.
characters.name: Ganymede

characters.description: The primordial god of old age, encountered as an obstacle on Percy's search. A deceptively ordinary-seeming figure, he embodies the wearing-down of youth and strength and proves a dangerous adversary for a young hero to face.
characters.name: Gary

characters.description: The slippery, ill-tempered Old Man of the Sea, a minor sea god known for holding useful knowledge and for hating to give it up. Percy must corner and pin him to force out the answers he needs, a trial Percy has faced before.
characters.name: Nereus

recaps.text: In the first five books of the series, twelve-year-old Percy Jackson discovers that he is a demigod, the son of the sea god Poseidon, and finds refuge at Camp Half-Blood, a summer camp for children of the Greek gods. Over five summers he takes on a string of dangerous quests: he recovers Zeus's stolen master lightning bolt and clears his own name; he retrieves the Golden Fleece to heal the camp's poisoned boundary; he helps rescue the goddess Artemis and his friend Annabeth and gains new allies and losses along the way; and he ventures into the deadly Labyrinth as an ancient enemy stirs. Throughout, the Titan lord Kronos works to rise again by possessing the embittered demigod Luke Castellan and raising an army against Olympus. In the final book Percy leads the young demigods in the desperate battle for New York, a great prophecy is fulfilled, Luke sacrifices himself to destroy Kronos, and the gods offer Percy immortality, which he refuses. Alongside his closest companions, the daughter of Athena Annabeth Chase and the satyr Grover Underwood, Percy has since grown into a seasoned hero, older now and facing more ordinary worries about his future.

Percy Jackson, now a seventeen-year-old high-school senior, wants nothing more than a normal future: to graduate and attend New Rome University with his girlfriend, Annabeth Chase. But he learns that admission requires three letters of recommendation from the gods, which means doing the Olympians' bidding once more. His first opportunity arrives when Ganymede, the cupbearer of the gods, secretly comes to him in a panic: the sacred chalice he serves the gods from has gone missing, and if the other Olympians find out, the consequences could be dire. To earn his first recommendation letter, Percy agrees to recover the lost cup quietly, and he sets out on the search with Annabeth and his old friend Grover Underwood, hoping this quest proves simpler than the world-ending ones of his past.

characters.description: A demigod son of Poseidon and a seasoned young hero, brave, loyal, and quick with a joke even in the Underworld. With a great war against the Titans looming, he is drawn into a dangerous errand in the land of the dead and teams up with two other powerful demigods to carry it out.
characters.name: Percy Jackson

characters.description: A fierce demigod daughter of Zeus who now serves as a Huntress of the goddess Artemis, sworn off aging and romance and gifted with fighting skill and command of Zeus's lightning. Bold and blunt, she joins Percy and Nico on the quest through the Underworld.
characters.name: Thalia

characters.description: A brooding demigod son of Hades who can raise and command the dead and travel through shadows. At home in the Underworld in a way the others are not, he is a natural, if uneasy, guide for a mission into his father's realm.
characters.name: Nico di Angelo

characters.description: The queen of the Underworld and wife of Hades, a goddess of spring bound for part of each year to the land of the dead. It is she who secretly summons the three demigods and sets them their task, wanting the trouble resolved before her husband learns of it.
characters.name: Persephone

characters.description: The grim lord of the Underworld and god of the dead, brother of Zeus and Poseidon. Proud and easily angered, he has had a powerful new weapon forged for the coming war, and its loss threatens both his pride and the balance of the conflict.
characters.name: Hades

characters.description: An ancient Titan, one of the immortal enemies of the gods rising for the war against Olympus. Powerful and full of old hatred, he stands in the demigods' way as they pursue the stolen weapon, a formidable foe for three young heroes to face in the Underworld.
characters.name: Iapetus

characters.description: A demigod son of the goddess Nemesis who has thrown in with the Titans' cause, resentful of the gods for neglecting minor deities and their children. Cunning and dangerous, he is caught up in the theft the demigods are sent to undo.
characters.name: Ethan Nakamura

recaps.ending: The three demigods recover the stolen Stygian iron sword forged for Hades, keeping it out of the Titan army's hands as the great war looms. The turning point comes when Percy plunges the Titan Iapetus into the River Lethe; stripped of every memory, the Titan loses his malice along with his past, and the newly harmless being is nicknamed Bob. The thief Ethan Nakamura's scheme fails, and the weapon is returned to Hades. Nico di Angelo stays behind in the Underworld with his father, still finding his place there, while Percy and Thalia return to the world above. The victory is small against the scale of the coming conflict, but it denies the enemy a dangerous prize and leaves an unexpected, gentle Titan wandering the land of the dead.
recaps.in_short: In this short adventure set during the war against the Titans, Persephone secretly summons three demigods, Percy Jackson, Thalia, and Nico di Angelo, to the Underworld. A powerful new sword of Stygian iron, forged for Hades and able to command the dead, has been stolen, and it must be recovered before it strengthens the enemy. The trio pursue the thief and clash with the demigod Ethan Nakamura and the ancient Titan Iapetus, who has taken the blade. In a desperate fight Percy hurls Iapetus into the River Lethe, the river of forgetfulness, which wipes away the Titan's memory and his hatred. Reborn blank and gentle, the confused Titan is given the harmless name Bob. The demigods retrieve Hades' sword and return it, denying it to the Titan army. Nico remains in the Underworld with his father, and Percy leaves with the war against the Titans still ahead of him.

recaps.text: In the first four books of the series, Percy Jackson learns he is a demigod son of Poseidon and finds a home at Camp Half-Blood, the sanctuary for children of the Greek gods. Over successive quests he recovers Zeus's stolen master lightning bolt, retrieves the Golden Fleece to heal the camp's borders, which also restores his friend Thalia, daughter of Zeus, to life, and helps rescue the goddess Artemis and his friend Annabeth, after which Thalia joins the immortal Hunters of Artemis. Along the way the lonely, powerful Nico di Angelo is revealed to be a son of Hades. Beneath all these adventures, the exiled Titan lord Kronos is gathering strength and followers to overthrow the gods, working through the embittered demigod Luke Castellan, and by now Kronos has taken physical form. With open war between the Titans and Olympus drawing near, both sides scramble for any advantage, and the demigods know a decisive conflict is coming.

With the war against the Titans looming, Persephone, the queen of the Underworld, secretly calls three demigods down to the land of the dead: Percy Jackson, the Huntress Thalia, and Nico di Angelo, son of Hades. A powerful new sword has been forged for Hades from Stygian iron, a blade said to be able to command the souls of the dead, and it has been stolen. Persephone wants the three heroes to recover it quietly and quickly, before it can be turned against Olympus in the coming battle and before the theft causes more trouble. Reluctant allies with very different tempers, the trio set out through the dangers of the Underworld to track down the missing weapon and whoever took it.

characters.description: Captain of the Rocinante, now decades older and working contract enforcement for the Transport Union out in the colony systems. Grayer, slower, and tired of being the man who turns up when something goes wrong, he is quietly planning to hand the ship over and retire with Naomi. His instinct for making decisions on principle and worrying about the consequences afterward has not aged out of him.
characters.name: James Holden

characters.description: The Rocinante's engineer and Holden's partner of thirty years, one of the most respected technical minds in the union's orbit. She has spent decades building the systems that keep traffic through the gates working, and she has agreed with Holden that it is time to stop. Careful, patient, and better than anyone aboard at seeing the shape of a problem before it arrives.
characters.name: Naomi Nagata

characters.description: A former Martian Marine, now the Rocinante's ranking soldier and the person Holden and Naomi intend to leave the ship to. She is old for the work and knows it, still trains in powered armor, and has spent her career being underestimated by people who then have to fight her.
characters.name: Bobbie Draper

characters.description: The Rocinante's pilot, a Martian who has been flying the same ship for three decades and has watched his home planet empty out through the gates. Divorced, sentimental, and reluctant to think too hard about what he will do when the crew he has built his life around finally breaks up.
characters.name: Alex Kamal

characters.description: The Rocinante's mechanic, apparently unchanged by thirty years, still direct to the point of bluntness and still organized entirely around protecting the people he has decided are his. He has no particular interest in what happens to him and a great deal of interest in what happens to the crew.
characters.name: Amos Burton

characters.description: The Rocinante's technician, once the daughter of an industrial dynasty and once Holden's enemy. The illegal implants she used decades ago left her with a degenerative condition that gets steadily worse; she manages it with drugs and stubbornness, does her work, and does not discuss it more than she has to. Amos is her closest tie to the crew.
characters.name: Clarissa Mao

characters.description: President of the Transport Union, the Belter-led authority that governs all traffic through the ring gates and has become the effective third power of humanity alongside Earth and Mars. She built her career on ships and stations rather than politics, and she rules an institution she does not entirely trust herself to be running.
characters.name: Camina Drummer

characters.description: A senior figure in the Transport Union and Drummer's husband, based away from her in the union's operational sprawl. Well liked, well connected among Belter crews, and practiced at moving people and cargo without anyone official noticing.
characters.name: Saba

characters.description: A Laconian naval officer, young, disciplined, and thoroughly a product of the system that raised him. He believes the empire he serves is a rational and merciful improvement on the chaos it replaces, and he has been given his first independent command with a family waiting for him and everything to prove.
characters.name: Santiago Singh

characters.description: The ranking Laconian admiral in the field, commanding the empire's most powerful warship. A pragmatist rather than a zealot, he is more interested in what an occupation costs than in what it symbolizes, and he is willing to be patient in ways his subordinates are not.
characters.name: Anton Trejo

characters.description: The Laconian officer responsible for security in the occupation, methodical and unillusioned about what holding a station full of hostile people actually requires. He does his job precisely and offers his commander advice that his commander does not always want.
characters.name: Overstreet

characters.description: The Martian admiral who took a third of his navy's fleet through the gates a generation ago and vanished. He has spent the intervening decades on the world of Laconia building something out of the alien technology found there, and he now presents himself as the answer to humanity's disorder: a single authority, permanent and unopposable.
characters.name: Winston Duarte

characters.description: Patriarch of Freehold, a colony that has refused to register its ships or accept Transport Union authority over the gate. Proud, self-reliant, and prepared to argue that a world's independence is worth more than access to the rest of humanity.
characters.name: Payne Houston

recaps.ending: The Medina uprising and the Rocinante's escape happen together. Saba's underground takes its moment, the ship is fought free of the station, and a Laconian destroyer is taken with it. Governor Singh, whose reprisals had by then cost hundreds of lives, is killed as the rising unfolds, and Admiral Trejo takes direct control and immediately reverses the harshest of his policies. Clarissa Mao dies during the escape: she pushes her ruined body past what her implants and her illness will tolerate in order to keep the ship alive, and does not survive it. Holden trades himself for the rest: he surrenders to the Laconians in exchange for the Rocinante being let go and Medina spared further punishment, and is taken to Laconia as Duarte's prisoner. Bobbie Draper takes command of the Rocinante, with Alex and Amos aboard. Naomi goes into hiding and begins organizing the resistance in earnest. Drummer, having publicly surrendered the Transport Union to preserve it, is left as a figurehead inside an empire she is secretly working against. Laconia now holds Sol, Medina and the gate network, and the weapon Trejo used in the ring space has drawn the attention of something on the other side of the gates: ships are vanishing in transit, and everyone in the ring space briefly lost consciousness at once.
recaps.in_short: Thirty years after the founding of the Transport Union, the aging Rocinante crew are working out their retirement, with Bobbie Draper set to take the ship. Then Laconia arrives. Winston Duarte, the Martian admiral who took a fleet through the gates a generation ago, has spent the intervening decades building warships out of alien technology, and his flagship walks into the ring space and takes Medina Station without a fight. Sol falls next; the Transport Union's combined fleet is disabled and destroyed, and President Drummer surrenders to preserve what she can. Governor Santiago Singh administers occupied Medina with the conviction that firmness now means peace later, and his escalating reprisals convert a resentful station into a resistance. Holden is arrested, Naomi goes underground, and Saba's cell builds toward a rising. When it comes, the Rocinante fights free with a captured Laconian destroyer, but Clarissa Mao dies making the escape possible and Holden surrenders himself to buy it. He is taken to Laconia as Duarte's prisoner, Bobbie commands the ship, and Laconia rules humanity, having just attracted the notice of whatever killed the builders of the gates.

recaps.text: Previously: the crew of the Rocinante spent a decade at the center of every crisis in the solar system, from the alien protomolecule's destruction of the station Eros to the opening of the ring gates and the thousand-plus worlds behind them. The Belter revolutionary Marco Inaros threw asteroids at Earth and killed billions before his Free Navy was destroyed at the ring gate. Out of that settlement came the Transport Union, a Belter-led authority governing all traffic through the gates from Medina Station, which gave the Belt a permanent stake in the new worlds. One loose end was never resolved: a rogue Martian admiral, Winston Duarte, had taken roughly a third of the Martian navy and a sample of the protomolecule through the gates and disappeared into a system called Laconia. This book opens roughly thirty years later. Humanity has settled hundreds of worlds. Mars has been hollowed out by emigration, Earth is still recovering, and the union polices the gates. The Rocinante's crew are old: Holden and Naomi are preparing to retire and hand the ship to Bobbie Draper, with Alex still flying, Amos apparently unchanged, and Clarissa Mao aboard as a technician whose old implants are slowly killing her. Camina Drummer is president of the Transport Union. Nobody in Sol has heard anything from Laconia in thirty years.

The Rocinante is enforcing Transport Union rules at Freehold, a colony world that has refused to register its ships or acknowledge the union's authority over its gate. Holden settles it with a judgment designed to punish without killing anyone: Freehold loses its ships and its access to the gate for a generation, which its patriarch Payne Houston regards as a death sentence for the colony's independence and Holden regards as mercy. The crew's real preoccupation is retirement. Holden and Naomi mean to leave, Bobbie is to take the ship, and nobody is entirely comfortable saying so out loud. Meanwhile, thirty years of silence from the Laconia system is ending: Duarte's project there is finished, and the ships it produced are moving.

Laconia arrives. A single warship of a class nothing in human space can match enters the ring space, absorbs everything the Transport Union's defenses can throw at it without meaningful damage, and takes Medina Station. Admiral Trejo installs Santiago Singh as governor with orders to make the transition orderly. Singh, on his first independent command, believes that a firm, rational administration will convince Medina's population that the empire is an improvement, and treats compliance as something he can simply require. Holden and Naomi are on Medina when it falls. Drummer, at the head of a union that has just discovered its fleet is obsolete, has to decide what surrender is worth.

Laconia takes the rest of humanity. The Laconian flagship moves into Sol, where the combined fleets of Earth, Mars and the Transport Union meet it and are effectively destroyed without inflicting damage in return. Drummer publicly capitulates in order to keep the union intact and its people alive, a decision that costs her most of what she believed about herself. On Medina, Holden is arrested and held; Naomi avoids capture and disappears into the station's Belter infrastructure. Singh's administration begins to grind: rationing, registration, curfews, and the steady discovery that a population which cannot fight can still refuse. Saba starts assembling an underground out of union crews and Medina locals.

The occupation turns violent. Sabotage and an attack on Laconian personnel push Singh into reprisals he justifies as necessary, and each one recruits for the resistance. He orders a demonstration of force that kills civilians, alienates his own security staff, and destroys whatever consent his administration had. Trejo, away with the fleet, becomes increasingly concerned about the cost of what his governor is doing. Naomi, moving unseen through the station, works with Saba's cell; Holden, in custody, is a symbol both sides want to control. Amos, Alex, Bobbie and Clarissa keep the Rocinante hidden and prepare for the moment the station rises.

The underground commits to a rising timed against the Rocinante's escape. The plan requires the ship to be fought out of a defended station, the resistance to seize enough of Medina to cover it, and everyone involved to accept losses. Singh, isolated and convinced that only greater severity can restore order, prepares a response that would be catastrophic for the station's population, and his own officers begin weighing what their oaths actually require. Naomi, Saba and the crew make their final arrangements, knowing that whatever happens, none of them will be going back to the lives they were arguing about a few months earlier.

Medina rises and the Rocinante fights free, taking a Laconian destroyer with it. Singh is killed as the uprising unfolds, and Trejo assumes direct control and rescinds his worst policies. Clarissa Mao keeps the ship alive through the escape by driving her failing body past what it can survive, and dies. Holden surrenders himself to the Laconians in exchange for the Rocinante being released and Medina spared reprisals, and is taken to Laconia as Duarte's prisoner. Bobbie takes command of the ship with Alex and Amos aboard; Naomi stays behind the lines to organize the resistance. Drummer remains the public head of a Transport Union that now answers to Laconia, and quietly supports the underground. Humanity is under a single government for the first time. And the weapon Laconia used in the ring space has been noticed by something on the far side of the gates: ships have started vanishing in transit, and for one moment every mind in the ring space went dark at once.
